title: Malicorne to Henri III, Niort, 21 April 1586: cipher letter in BnF fr. 15572 ff. 162-164 (Malicorne's cipher)

documents.route: Jean de Chourses, sieur de Malicorne, governor of Poitou (Niort) → Henri III

plaintext.source: A contemporary decipherment in the margin of f. 163r beside stretches A and B (brackx2026/margin_f163r.txt); B's margin is partly illegible between 'argent' and 'descouvertes'.

system.notes: distinct_symbols measured on texts/f162r_transcription.txt (labels, including the | divider). Key: brackx2026/key_r2.txt.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherment in the margin of f. 163r (stretches A and B); Tomokiyo (Cryptiana, henryiii) gives the key table only. No other reading found (Brackx, issue #92).

conditions.human_role: Contributed: Michael Brackx (issue #92, 22-23 Oct 2026) transcribed and decoded the letter with Claude Code outside the project; the project asked for the aligned decode under the read bar, measured and reviewed it.
tools: Brackx beam decoder over label values with a French character 5-gram (external)

solution.what: Michael Brackx (issue #92): Tomokiyo's henryiii page ('Malycorne's Cipher') gives the key table, no reading; no other reading found in this repository or on the web.
Gallica full-size IIIF images of BnF fr. 15572, canvases 169 right to 173 right.
Tomokiyo's table encoded as labels with values; nulls and the digraph and word signs (de, la, le, que, sur, ss, mm, ll, nn, ee) kept.
Every cipher line transcribed sign by sign from deskewed full-size line crops; the f. 163r margin read at full size; a line-by-line proofread corrected about 30 lines.

Beam search over each label's allowed values under a French character 5-gram; three per-page keys merged into one label set and pruned one value at a time (labels with two or more values 43 -> 13, -0.5 points coverage); about 40 relabels from contact sheets; a decoder bug that skipped lines beginning with '#' fixed.
Corpus-word coverage over all pages posted as 76.5% (shuffled keys 37.8-49.8%).

Brackx's correction to the language model (only Gutenberg 48529 of 48529-48531 was Montaigne): rebuilt from the Essais I-III (48529, 49168, 58801), page coverage falls from 76.5% to 72.3% (shuffled 32.5-47.7%); key and readings unchanged, crib A stays at 97.6%.

Crib B restated: the posted 72.8% for B ll. 4-14 cannot be reproduced (cipher rows and crib text not recorded); under a stated definition (the legible margin words against cipher rows 4-8) it is 79.3%, against 15-24% for shuffled keys.

Aligned decode of f. 162r and f. 163r (transcription, value per sign, decoded line, not edited by hand) and readings in the decode's spelling with English. Departures from the raw decode recorded: 6 hand-chosen readings on two-valued labels (Lusignan, ceulx, ici, Cossart, tramee, ce; 7 letters, 0.6% of f. 162r's letters and 0.7% of f. 163r's, under the 3% look-alike limit) and 3 margin-carried words on f. 163r B (i'auois, charbonnieres, descouuertes).

Measured with research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.measure: f. 163r A 0.727 (one sentence, confirmed by the margin: read in part); f. 162r 0.622 and f. 163r B 0.694 (phrases between gaps: decoded, not read). Reviewed as sentences (grade B) by Claude Opus 5.5. The other four pages are not yet given; their aligned decode and a sign-shape legend were requested from the contributor.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's key table, corrected by Michael Brackx and checked against the contemporary margin decipherment of f. 163r (crib A 97.6%, crib B 79.3%), applied to the figures; f. 163r A reads as one margin-confirmed sentence.

texts.label: f. 163r, stretch A
texts.summary: The credence: the rest 'consists in the credence of the bearer and the said articles'.

reading_review.note: One complete sentence, confirmed word for word by the margin decipherment; 3 holes in 11 words.

texts.label: f. 162r
texts.summary: Malicorne to Henri III from Niort, 21 April 1586: the plots against Lusignan have failed; Villeluisant's raid cut two Protestant companies to pieces near Sanxay and brought their captains and ensigns to Niort.

reading_review.note: Phrases between gaps: 65 holes in 167 words; the sentences do not build.

texts.label: f. 163r, stretch B
texts.summary: The two enterprises Malicorne had against Lusignan, one plotted at the charcoal-burners', were discovered.

reading_review.note: Phrases between gaps; three words carried by the margin; the margin between 'argent' and 'descouvertes' is mostly illegible.
